discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism; the experimental discovery that made it possible remains unrecognised. The 2012 observation of a 125 GeV scalar by ATLAS and CMS, independently and with overwhelming significance, required detectors of unprecedented granularity, speed and radiation hardness. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders of CMS, Virdee also architect of its crystal calorimeter) conceived these instruments in the late 1980s, defined their physics-driven designs, notably the photon and lepton precision that made H to gamma-gamma and H to four leptons visible, and led them through construction. Over a decade of measurements since has established the boson's couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and now muons, confirming the Standard Model's mass-generation mechanism and anchoring every search for physics beyond it. Their individual vision was decisive for this landmark.
